subject: Business Models
title: Luckin Coffee: Fabricated Sales
description: A fast breakdown of Luckin Coffee: Fabricated Sales for builders.

hook.text: Luckin opened 4,500 stores in 18 months to beat Starbucks in China. Then it admitted faking $310M in sales.

buildup.text: Luckin raised billions promising to dominate China's coffee market through speed and technology.

discovery.text: Employees fabricated transactions using personal purchases and inflated delivery orders to meet growth targets.

twist.text: Luckin survived the scandal. Under new management, it actually became profitable and now has 16,000+ stores.

climax.text: Luckin is a rare case: a fraud that, once cleaned up, revealed a viable business underneath the deception.

punchline.text: Faked $310M, survived, now actually works. The fraud was unnecessary.

quiz.question: What makes Luckin Coffee unusual among corporate fraud cases?
options: The underlying business was actually viable after the fraud was cleaned up
